title: Get Gorilla Glutes (Best MASS Building Exercises)
summary: His three favorite glute-biased compounds: close-stance safety-bar box squats, full-range hip thrusts with a down-and-in bar path, and forward-leaning Bulgarian split squats. He takes a middle position between 'just squat and deadlift' and glute-specialist isolation: heavy squats and deadlifts build the most mass, and glute-biased compounds that force glute use are the best supplement.
claims: He sits between 'just squat and deadlift' bros and glute specialists: he built big glutes with compounds, but glute-biased compounds also help
The close-stance safety-bar box squat forces a deadlift-like bottom position, heavily loading glutes, hamstrings and erectors, so it can replace a floor pull for glutes
Without a safety squat bar you can use a low-bar position, but it isn't quite the same lift
Set the box at parallel (about knee height), angled like a diamond pointing to the rack, with feet either side as narrow as your conventional deadlift stance
Despite his knee problems with narrow stances, this lift doesn't bother his knee tendons, and it carries over to the deadlift and squat; like a good morning with more glute
Let the safety bar push your torso forward instead of fighting to stay upright; the movement becomes a semi-knee-flexion hip hinge
Box squats here are touch-and-go: never rock back on the box with a safety bar, control the tempo and never bounce off the box to move more weight
Soreness is not a perfect growth signal but shows a muscle was stressed more than usual; if you can't feel your glutes on squats, this lift will fix that
For glute hypertrophy the hip thrust beats the glute bridge because it has more range of motion; bridges suit deadlift accessory work
On hip thrusts don't cut the range of motion; lower until the plates touch the floor, where the glutes work most; the top squeeze does little
Use a relatively close stance on hip thrusts to allow knee flexion and more range, not a wide frog stance with tiny hip movements
Don't manipulate general lifts to bias glutes, like pushing the butt back on squats; choose movements that force glute use
Put the bar on the hip crease with a pad for comfort and stability so it doesn't roll
Focus on the knees, not the hips, on hip thrusts: the bar travels down and in, then up and out, which adds hamstrings and a deeper glute stretch; a straight up-and-down path does little
Hip thrusts: sets of 10-15 with some reps in reserve; you can go to failure safely, but never cut range of motion
He hated lunges after a football coach made the team do lunge laps, but has reintroduced Bulgarian split squats, partly to target his VMO
Trying to isolate the glutes is like isolating the lower back; train the muscles around them and the glutes come along
In a Bulgarian split squat always keep the knee tracking the same direction as the foot
For glute bias in split squats, start upright and let the torso lean onto the thigh as you descend, a pendulum in-and-out path; don't start the rep already leaning or rounded
Keep body weight on the outside top of the front foot and push off the pinky toe to avoid rotating into the quads
Use Bulgarian split squats as a secondary movement with modest weight for 10-15 reps; failure and drop sets are fine and the forward lean lowers knee stress
Heavy squats and deadlifts remain the best glute mass builders; glute size is partly genetic, but anyone combining them with glute-biased lifts will grow a big butt
exercises: Close-stance safety squat bar box squat
parallel box, deadlift-width stance, let the bar tip you forward, touch-and-go, no rocking or bouncing
deadlift-like bottom position forces glutes, hamstrings and erectors; easy on his knees
bar on hip crease with pad, close stance, plates touch the floor, bar path down-and-in then up-and-out, 10-15 reps
more range of motion than a glute bridge
knee tracks foot, lean torso onto thigh during descent, weight on outer front foot, 10-15 reps
glute bias with low knee stress; secondary movement
